name: Substantia nigra
summary: A pigmented band of neurons between the crus cerebri and the tegmentum of the midbrain, black in fresh specimens because its dopaminergic neurons contain neuromelanin. The pars compacta sends dopamine to the striatum (nigrostriatal pathway) and dies in Parkinson disease; the pars reticulata is a GABAergic output nucleus like the internal pallidum, controlling the thalamus and, through the superior colliculus, saccades. Its loss produces bradykinesia, rigidity, rest tremor and postural instability, and it is the site of the swallow-tail sign lost on susceptibility-weighted MRI.

anatomy.location: Ventral midbrain tegmentum along the whole length of the midbrain, dorsal to the crus cerebri and ventral to the red nucleus and medial lemniscus, extending rostrally to the subthalamus.

subdivisions.name: Pars compacta
subdivisions.note: densely packed dopaminergic neurons projecting to the striatum; degenerates in Parkinson disease, ventrolateral tier first

subdivisions.name: Pars reticulata
subdivisions.note: GABAergic output neurons projecting to the thalamus and superior colliculus; functionally continuous with the internal pallidum

function: Dopaminergic modulation of striatal activity enabling movement initiation and reward learning (pars compacta); tonic inhibition of thalamus and superior colliculus controlling movement and saccades (pars reticulata).

bestView.label: substantia nigra behind the crus cerebri at the level of the red nucleus
pigmented band between crus and tegmentum

imaging.normalAppearance: A dark band behind the crus on T2 and SWI (iron), best seen at the level of the red nucleus; the dorsolateral nigral hyperintensity (swallow tail) on high-resolution SWI is lost in Parkinson disease, and neuromelanin-sensitive T1 shows reduced signal. Structural MRI is otherwise normal in idiopathic disease.

pathology.finding: Loss of the swallow-tail sign on SWI and of neuromelanin signal in the pars compacta; dopamine transporter SPECT shows reduced putaminal uptake.
Paramedian midbrain lesion involving the nigra and adjacent structures: contralateral parkinsonism or hemiballismus with a third nerve palsy (Benedikt).
Midbrain atrophy (hummingbird sign) with nigral involvement.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Axial SWI and T2 through the midbrain; dopamine transporter imaging

lesionEffects.deficit: Bradykinesia, rigidity, rest tremor, postural instability
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of dopaminergic pars compacta neurons (symptoms appear after ~60% loss)
Mesolimbic dopamine from the adjacent ventral tegmental area

lesionEffects.deficit: Hemiballismus or dystonia with tegmental lesions

examination: Finger tapping with decrement, rapid alternating movements, foot tapping
Rigidity at the wrist with activation
Pull test and gait with arm swing
Ask about anosmia, REM sleep behavior disorder and constipation
pearls: Asymmetric onset of bradykinesia with rest tremor and a good levodopa response is Parkinson disease; symmetric onset with early falls suggests an atypical syndrome
Neuroleptics block the same dopamine receptors and mimic nigral loss
